messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for private-vpc-controlplane/garnet-eu-west-1 — 'agent-heartbeat-missing' (severity: p1). Notifying #incidents and oncall.

pagerduty: Page sent to alice.sre (on-call). Incident key: PD-98342. Escalation policy: oncall -> l2 -> infra.

alice.sre: ack'd. I'm on it. What's the impact?

incident-bot: Customers affected: Garnet Inc (private VPC). Observed: control plane hasn't received heartbeats from 3/3 onprem agents for last 4m. Control plane: connection count dropped to 0 for that customer.

alice.sre: ok. quick checks: control plane health dashboards? any deploys in last hour?

bob.infra: checking control plane metrics now. No platform-wide deploys in the last 2 hours. I see a spike in connection errors from eu-west-1 -> onprem egress: logs show TLS handshake failures and RSTs around 1777743170-1777743200.

frank.eng: I pulled the raw connection logs from the controlplane proxy: 
```
2026-03-15T10:52:31Z conn from 10.8.7.4:34912 -> agent.garnet.local:443 handshake failed: read tcp: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T10:52:44Z conn closed: broker->agent: write: connection reset by peer
```

carla.prod: Customer impact? Are they seeing errors in their app? Emily, can you reach out?

emily.cs: pinging Garnet SRE (oncall@Garnet) now. Will ask them to confirm agent state and if they've had network changes. ETA 5m.

alice.sre: Good. In parallel: can someone try to hit the agent health endpoint from our side? curl to the agent's public egress IP? If not, we need to ask customer to run checks.

bob.infra: Attempted curl via our egress in eu-west-1 -> timed out. Looks like their firewall/NAT may be dropping. I can see their ASN route still valid.

devon.oncall: I'm coming in for L2 triage. @alice.sre handing off. I have runbooks open. First steps: 1) confirm agent process, 2) check local firewall rules/NAT, 3) verify control plane cert acceptance.

alice.sre: Handoff notes: control plane saw all 3 agents go silent at ~1777743165. No recent deploys. Logs show handshake RSTs. Customer contacted. Devon taking lead.

devon.oncall: @emily.cs can you ask Garnet to run these commands on their on-prem router/host and paste results: 
```
curl -v http://localhost:9090/health || curl -v https://agent.garnet.local:443/health
sudo systemctl status redwood-agent.service || sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200
sudo iptables -L -n -v | grep -E "443|9090" || sudo ufw status verbose
```

emily.cs: Sent to Garnet SRE. They replied: "we started a scheduled firewall rule push for maintenance around 10:50 UTC accidentally targeted the agent subnet; rollbacking now." They say they'll confirm once rollback completes. ETA ~3m.

frank.eng: If the rollback is true, we should be prepared to accept reconnections. I'll tail control plane stream to watch for reconnects: `kubectl logs -f controlplane-proxy -n redwood --selector customer=garnet`

bob.infra: Also seeing a short burst of NAT translation errors on the guard gateway: `nat: no available ports` around same time. Could be that their outbound pool exhausted during the firewall push.

emily.cs: Update from Garnet: they rolled back rule, and are starting agent restart. They ran `sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent` on one node and got: `Job for redwood-agent.service failed because the control process exited with error code.` They're investigating.

devon.oncall: OK ask them to paste `sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200` output. Also ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect agent.garnet.local:443 -servername agent.garnet.local -brief` and post TLS handshake details.

emily.cs: Got logs from Garnet SRE: 
```
Mar 15 10:52:28 host1 redwood-agent[2145]: tls: handshake error: EOF
Mar 15 10:52:30 host1 redwood-agent[2145]: connection closed by remote host
Mar 15 10:53:02 host1 redwood-agent[2145]: starting up
```
They also ran openssl and it shows `CONNECTED(00000003)` but then `write:errno=104` (connection reset by peer).

carla.prod: Noted. If agent is failing handshake and control plane shows RST, could be an MTU or middlebox dropping large packets. Any path MTU issues lately?

bob.infra: I ran packet captures on the egress and see SACK resets, likely a middlebox. Also noticed their egress IP had ephemeral port reuse issues. Suggesting Garnet to try a simple tcpdump and check for MSS/MTU blackhole.

emily.cs: Garnet ran `tcpdump -nn -s0 -w - 'port 443'` and forwarded a pcap to us via secure link. Devon, can you check?

devon.oncall: Downloading pcap now. Quick scan: multiple SYNs, SYN-ACKs, then immediate RST from intermediate IP 198.51.100.45 (their corporate firewall). This matches firewall rollback comment. It looks like the rollback only partially applied and a policy is still dropping long-lived TLS connections.

frank.eng: Given that, we should route calls for Garnet through our fallback proxy path that uses a different egress (bgp-peering -> dedicated-proxy) to restore control plane connectivity while customer fixes firewall. I can flip a smart-routing override.

alice.sre: Approve fallback? Impact: uses burst capacity on dedicated proxies for Garnet for ~30m, extra cost billed to account.

carla.prod: Approve. Notify billing and the customer. Emily, please tell Garnet we're going to create a temporary bypass and will coordinate.

emily.cs: Notified Garnet: "We will create a temporary routing bypass through Redwood dedicated proxies to restore agent heartbeats while you finish firewall rollback. This will not touch data plane paths for customer traffic, only control channel." They gave verbal OK.

bob.infra: I pushed a routing override: `redwoodctl routing apply --customer garnet --route override-proxy-eu-west` — change propagated to controlplane edge in 6s. Watching for reconnects.

frank.eng: I'm seeing agent reconnection attempts at 1777743500. Control plane logs show successful TLS handshake at 1777743512 for host1. :white_check_mark:

devon.oncall: Great. Confirmed 3/3 agents reconnected by 1777743550. I'm going to monitor for 10m, then start de-escalation. Handing off to alice for post-incident tasks.

alice.sre: I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates. Action items: 1) improve pager content to include quick fallback runbook, 2) add a synthetic control-plane check for Garnet to detect partial firewall rollbacks, 3) billing ticket to notify of fallback charges. Filing ticket RN-1129.

carla.prod: Also schedule a follow-up call with Garnet to review maintenance procedures. Assign to Emily.

emily.cs: Meeting scheduled with Garnet SRE for 2026-03-16 09:00 UTC.

devon.oncall: Closing active page in PD and marking incident resolved. PD note: temporary route used, reconnects successful, root cause: partial firewall push at customer side causing TLS resets.

incident-bot: Incident PD-98342 marked resolved by devon.oncall at 1777743625.

alice.sre: Thanks team. I'll draft the incident summary and link RN-1129 when ready.

emily.cs: Customer confirmed no application impact beyond agent disconnect window (~3m). They thanked us for quick mitigation. :pray: 

frank.eng: small follow-up: I'll add a health-check that tolerates transient firewall pushes (exponential backoff + jitter) to reduce noisy disconnects. PR: github.com/redwood/agent/pull/578.

alice.sre: nice. Closing thread after PM notes added. :white_check_mark:
